key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in perovskite films act as degradation nucleation sites, and they can be rapidly detected with microscopy plus machine learning before device failure accelerates.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a fast, non-invasive pre-screening tool to flag unstable perovskite films early, supporting scalable manufacturing of more durable solar cells.
method: Nano-FTIR chemically identified impurity phases in wide-bandgap perovskite films.
High-resolution reflected-light microscopy captured impurity-rich regions non-invasively.
Machine learning image analysis quantified impurity density within seconds for rapid screening.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress and degradation-tracking experiments showed that failure begins at impurity–perovskite interfaces, and films with higher impurity density degraded earlier and faster.
watch_item: The approach needs robust calibration across film compositions, imaging setups, and manufacturing conditions to avoid false positives or missed impurities.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
